source.authors: Anderson CM, Wisenden BD, Craig CA, Stockwell CA
source.title: Consistent Antipredator Behavioral Responses among Populations of Red River Pupfish with Disparate Predator Communities

value: conspecific skin alarm cue significantly reduced post-stimulus water column position relative to water control (Cue F1,140 = 21.170, p < 0.001); Population effects not significant
units: categorical (ANCOVA effect of cue on position in water column)
method: individual female fish in 37 L aquaria; 10 mL dose of conspecific skin extract (skin blended and diluted to 1 cm2 skin per 10 mL) or dechlorinated tap water at 10 ppt salinity control injected; water column position recorded every 10 s for 5 min before and 5 min after the stimulus
conditions: wild-sourced: females collected from five Red River sites (Table 1 n = 33, 22, 38, 38, 29; 160 fish) and shipped to NDSU, held in 1135 L population-specific outdoor tanks, at least 20 h acclimation before trials, trials June to August 2020; within each block two females from each population were randomly assigned to the two treatments; analysis dropped one hyperactive fish and eight trials with no pre-stimulus movement, and per-treatment n after exclusions is not given; same-section activity result: a Cue x Pre-stimulus activity interaction (F1,140 = 9.90; p = 0.002); Cue x Pre-stimulus behaviour interaction not significant for water column position; Population direct and interactive effects not significant for either variable; skin-donor number not stated
quote: Alarm cue caused a significant reduction in the post-stimulus water column position (Cue F1,140 = 21.170, p < 0.001; Table 2B), but the direct and interactive effects of Population were not significant (Table 2B, Figure 2B).
note: Classification: behavioural_response, a water-column position (freezing/refuge-type) change after a chemical cue with a water control; no other modality in the design.
